title: Session-duration-tiering-and-granular-billing-approach
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This playbook defines a practical, developer-focused pricing model for session-based workloads: Session Duration Tiering with Granular Billing (SDT-GB). It is intended for conversational and transactional products that measure cost across time, tokens, and session-level state (KV/embeddings footprint). The goal is to make consumption predictable for customers while enabling Redwood to account for warm capacity, KV cache residency, and tail latency premium.

Goals

- Provide a pricing model that aligns customer cost to the dominant drivers for server cost: active session time, memory footprint (KV/embeddings), and peak concurrency.
- Preserve clear unit economics for self-serve and enterprise customers without blocking advanced features (adaptive fidelity, prefetching).
- Offer an easy onramp (free / trial credits) and automated migration paths from per-token billing to SDT-GB for heavy session clients.

Scope

- Applies to hosted and dedicated deployments for session-oriented APIs (chat sessions, long-lived transactional sessions).
- Not in scope: pure embedding batch jobs, one-shot text generation without session state.

Definitions

- Active Session Time: wall-clock duration where a session is considered 'active' for pricing (from first request to TTL-based expiry or explicit close, with idle windows allowed).
- Held KV Footprint: bytes of KV/cache and per-session embeddings retained on serving nodes attributable to the session.
- Concurrency Window: the peak number of concurrent active sessions within a billing interval.

Pricing Model (high level)

1) Base session tiering (per-active-minute):
   - Tier A: 0–10 active minutes per billable session/month: $0.0008 / minute
   - Tier B: 10–120 active minutes per session/month: $0.00045 / minute
   - Tier C: >120 active minutes per session/month: $0.00018 / minute

   Rationale: higher-duration sessions benefit from decreasing per-minute rates because their KV residency amortizes warmup costs.

2) Memory surcharge (per-GB-hour):
   - Charged for average held KV Footprint per-session in GB-hours: $0.15 / GB-hour.

3) Concurrency premium (peak window multiplier):
   - If a customer's 95th-percentile peak concurrency in a billing period exceeds an entitlement threshold for their plan, a +10–40% multiplier applies to the base session minutes to reflect capacity reservation costs.

4) Token smoothing (optional):
   - Token consumption is still metered for high-variance workloads (e.g., long generative responses). We apply a token smoothing credit tied to session tier that offsets up to X% of token cost to avoid double-charging for long sessions.

Customer-facing examples

Example A — Lightweight chat agent
- 1,200 sessions/month, median active duration 2 minutes, KV footprint 5 MB average
- Billing = session-minutes * Tier A + memory surcharge (negligible) + no concurrency premium

Example B — Enterprise agent with long sessions
- 3,000 sessions/month, 1% of sessions exceed 180 minutes, avg KV footprint 250 MB, 95th-peak concurrency high
- Billing = majority of minutes in Tier B/C + memory surcharge (0.25 GB * hours) + concurrency multiplier (applies to minutes)

Technical telemetry & collection requirements

To support accurate billing the runtime must emit the following metrics per-customer (tagged by tenant_id and session_id):

- session.start_ts (ISO8601) and session.end_ts (ISO8601 or TTL expiry)
- session.idle_intervals: list of idle windows (start,end) to calculate billable active time
- session.kv_avg_bytes (sampled hourly)
- session.token_count_inbound, session.token_count_outbound (per-request counters)
- tenant.peak_concurrency_5m and tenant.peak_concurrency_95p (aggregation)

Telemetry contract (aggregation)

- Runtime emits raw events to the telemetry pipeline. Billing pipeline will ingest hourly aggregates per tenant and per session for the current billing window.
- Aggregator must produce stable hourly summaries with a watermark policy to handle late events (max 10-minute lateness).

Billing pipeline logic (sequence)

1) Ingest hourly aggregates for sessions and memory footprints.
2) Reconstruct per-session active-minutes with idle-window trimming and TTL rules.
3) Assign minutes to tiers and apply minute rates.
4) Compute memory GB-hours and add surcharge.
5) Compute peak concurrency and apply multiplier if above entitlement.

Configuration & thresholds (table)

| Setting key | Default | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------|
| session.idle_ttl_minutes | 15 | Idle window after which session is considered inactive for billing (customer can choose shorter with API flag) |
| session.max_backfill_lateness_minutes | 10 | Billing pipeline will accept late telemetry up to this threshold |
| concurrency.multiplier_threshold_95p | plan-dependent | Default entitlement per plan; overrideable for enterprise contracts |
| memory.surcharge_per_gb_hour | 0.15 | Default surcharge; negotiable for large enterprise commitments |

Migration & onboarding playbook (customer journeys)

1) Discovery: run consumption analysis for 30 days under current per-token model and SDT-GB simulated billing. Provide a comparative report.
2) Opt-in trial: enable SDT-GB in test tenant with sandbox credits for 60 days.
3) Contracting: if projected cost is within acceptable bounds, sign a plan that locks concurrency entitlement and memory surcharge floors.
4) Migrate: switch billing flag and run parallel billing for one month for validation.

Rollout timeline (recommended)

- Q2 2026: Pilot with 5 developer-focused customers (self-serve + API keys labeled trial-sdtgb).
- Q3 2026: Expand to Dedicated customers with a signed concurrency entitlement path.
- Q4 2026: GA for hosted customers with opt-in via Console and API toggle.

Rollout checkpoints (each checkpoint requires completion of the specific gate):

- Telemetry pipeline validated against 99.9% ingestion success for pilot tenants.
- Billing pipeline reconciliation differences <0.5% vs legacy per-token baseline over two consecutive weeks.
- Console UX for bill preview and per-session breakdown shipped.

Console UX & developer APIs

- Bill preview API: /v1/billing/preview?tenant_id=...&period=YYYY-MM returns estimated SDT-GB charges and per-session breakdown (first phase read-only).
- Admin toggle: flag to enable SDT-GB per-tenant.
- Console page: Top-level summary, 95p concurrency chart, heatmap of session durations, and a downloadable CSV for per-session charge breakdown.

API sample (bill preview response example)

{
  "tenant_id": "acme-corp-123",
  "period": "2026-03",
  "estimated_minutes": "124560",
  "estimated_memory_gb_hours": "23.4",
  "concurrency_multiplier": "1.10",
  "estimated_total": "$3,452.32"
}

Operational responsibilities and SLAs

- Product (owner): finalize rates, create commercial packaging for trial/enterprise tiers, and own customer-facing docs.
- Eng-runtime: emit session telemetry and surface KV footprint. SLA: 99.95% telemetry emission availability for billable metrics.
- Eng-platform (billing pipeline): reconcile against token-billing baseline. SLA: billing run complete within 6 hours after month close for pilot tenants.
- Finance: validate accounting treatment and tax implications for time-based charges.

Success metrics (KPI)

- Adoption rate: % of eligible session customers that opt into SDT-GB within 6 months of GA. Target: 25% by end of Q1 after GA.
- Revenue confidence: median monthly billing reconciliation delta vs legacy <1%.
- Developer satisfaction: NPS change for pilot customers +10 points on billing clarity survey.

Risks and mitigations

- Risk: Customers manipulate session TTLs to reduce billed active minutes.
  - Mitigation: Add server-side minimums (e.g., min billable active-minute granularity of 30s) and sampling-based fraud detection.
- Risk: Telemetry loss causing underbilling or disputes.
  - Mitigation: Provide bill previews and a 30-day dispute window; store raw telemetry snapshots with checksums and retention of 90 days.
- Risk: Complexity reduces self-serve adoption.
  - Mitigation: Default to per-token model for small accounts; enable SDT-GB only for accounts above a consumption threshold or by opt-in.

Open questions for exec review

- Should concurrency entitlement be sold as a firm reservation (higher price) or a soft threshold with overage multipliers?
- Do we offer a cap on monthly SDT-GB charges for enterprise contracts to remove billing volatility?

Appendix A — Contract wording (example clause)

"Customer agrees to be billed for active-session time and held KV footprint as measured by Redwood's telemetry. Active-session time excludes server-side idle periods beyond 15 minutes. Peak concurrency entitlements and memory surcharges are defined in the applicable order form."

Appendix B — Billing dispute flow (summary)

1) Customer files dispute with invoice reference.
2) Billing and platform run differential reconciliation within 3 business days.
3) If discrepancy >1% or $5k, escalate to finance and account exec for resolution within 10 business days.
